findings.title: Charge lookup builds SQL with an f-string
findings.explanation: charge_id comes from the API request and is interpolated into the SQL text, so a crafted id can read or modify other rows.
findings.suggestion: Use a parameter: db.execute("SELECT * FROM charges WHERE id = ?", (charge_id,)).

findings.title: Refund amount converted with float arithmetic
findings.explanation: int(float("1204.35") * 100) is 120434, so some refunds are one cent short. CLAUDE.md requires Decimal for money.
findings.suggestion: amount_cents = int(Decimal(amount) * 100), and reject amounts with more than two decimal places.

findings.title: Partial refunds can exceed the original charge
findings.explanation: The limit check ignores refunded_so_far, so two 40.00 refunds on a 50.00 charge both succeed.
findings.suggestion: Check refunded_so_far + amount_cents > charge["amount_cents"], and add a test with two partial refunds.

findings.title: Full card number written to the log
findings.explanation: charge["card_number"] is logged at INFO level; card numbers must never reach logs (PCI DSS).

structured_output.summary: Four blocking issues in refund_charge: SQL injection, float money, cumulative refund limit and card data in logs.
